entry.title: Integrating SAP Concur with SAP SuccessFactors using MDI
entry.content:
SAP Concur can be integrated with SAP SuccessFactors in several ways, ranging from traditional file-based interfaces to modern API-driven integrations. Each approach has its own strengths and trade-offs, making the optimal choice dependent on the customer's landscape, integration requirements, and long-term strategy.

This post builds on previously covered integration options and takes a deeper dive into the Master Data Integration (MDI) approach. MDI provides a standardized approach to maintaining consistent, high-quality master data between SAP SuccessFactors, SAP Concur, and other SAP solutions, making it a key component of SAP's cloud integration strategy.

Prerequisites

Before beginning the configuration, ensure the following foundational components are in place:

  • An active SAP BTP Commercial License (CPEA or PAYG contract) - Needed for subscribing to SAP Master Data Integration)
  • An SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central tenant configured as the employee data provider
  • An SAP Concur tenant with appropriate administrative access
  • Access to SAP Cloud Identity Services (Identity Authentication Service / Identity Provisioning Service)
  • Access to SAP Cloud ALM for monitoring (optional but highly recommended for Customer Monitoring)
  • The Master Data Integration Administrator and Intelligent Enterprise Suite (IES) Integrations Administrator role assigned in SAP Concur

Integration Steps

Step 1 — Set Up Integration Between SuccessFactors - Cloud identity services - Concur

Raise a support ticket through the Concur Support Portal or SAP Portal to configure your SAP IAS/IPS tenant. When raising the ticket, explicitly mention that you are implementing MDI with SAP Concur, as the relevant roles can be assigned at once.

  • If using ServiceNow, use component BNS-CON-MDI-UPS for SAP Concur Integration with SAP Master Data Integration Service
  • If using the Concur support tool, reference the issue as IPS Provisioning
  • Always include your SAP Customer Number in the ticket (see here for more details)

Once the Intelligent Enterprise Suite (IES) Integrations Administrator role has been assigned by Concur personnel, trigger the automation and adjust the IAS configuration as needed. In some cases, IAS acts as a proxy rather than a direct identity provider, and configuration adjustments — such as the Subject Name Identifier — may be required.

Step 2 — Review and Adjust IPS Jobs

Review the jobs automatically created in the Identity Provisioning Service (IPS) and adjust them as needed.

The following guides might be helpful in configuring the source and target systems.

IPS is primarily used to provision the "user core" — basic user information such as name, login ID, employee ID, and email address. Expense and Travel-related profile data (such as organizational units, ledger, and employee group) are populated by MDI in a later step.

Important: You will also need an IPS job to assign roles, including the Approver role — a permission that allows users to approve expense reports, typically granted to managers. This can be managed via a dedicated group in IPS, synchronized from SuccessFactors based on criteria such as job code.

User core and the Approver role cannot be assigned simultaneously if the user does not yet exist in Concur. Therefore, the IPS job will need to be re-run after MDI has populated the Expense-related data.

Step 3 — Configure SuccessFactors–MDI Integration

This step involves:

  • Creating a BTP Service Instance for SuccessFactors
  • Creating MDI subaccount and configuring it including a service instance creation (in case customer does not have MDI yet)
  • Configure Business Scenario - Workforce Replication from EC to SAP Master Data Integration
  • Establishing the correct field mapping in the SuccessFactors–MDI configuration
  • Starting the replication from SuccessFactors to MDI

Refer to the official SAP Help documentation on Integrating SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central with SAP Master Data Integration for detailed how-to guidance.

Step 4 — Create Formation Between MDI and SAP Concur (BTP)

In this step, create a formation in SAP BTP between the SAP Master Data Integration Service and SAP Concur Solutions to establish connectivity.

  • The MDI Tenant and Concur Tenant should be auto-discovered. If they are not, raise a support case.
  • Two communication paths are established:
    • Concur → MDI Communication
    • BDO (Business Data Orchestration) → Concur Communication

Refer to the SAP Help documentation on Creating a Formation Between the SAP Master Data Integration Service and SAP Concur Solutions to Establish Connectivity for step-by-step instructions.

Step 5 — Configure SAP Cloud ALM (CALM) Monitoring

Set up SAP Cloud ALM in SAP BTP and activate monitoring for SAP Concur.

This step is essential for ongoing visibility into synchronization status and errors.

Step 6 — Field Mapping and Role Assignment

If the Master Data Integration Administrator role has not yet been assigned in SAP Concur, raise a support case to request the assignment.

This role  provides access to the Field Mapping configuration page in SAP Concur, where you can:

  • Define the mapping of ODM fields to Concur fields
  • Apply Implementation Codes, Conversion Codes, or Value Mappings as required

Review the Default Field Mapping documentation to understand out-of-the-box mappings and determine any custom mappings required for your organization.

Step 7 — Configure Business Data Orchestration (BDO) Distribution Model

In this step:

  • Create a Distribution Model for the existing Workforce Person object in the BDO service
  • Configure the distribution model by setting:
    • Activate the BDO distribution model to start the replication
    • Business Object (Workforce Person)
    • Filters (e.g., object selection criteria)
    • Frequency (scheduling for replication)

Step 8 — Initial Test Run

Before triggering a full load:

  • Add only a few employee IDs to the Object Selection Filter in the BDO service
  • Trigger IPS job to create "user core" before triggering MDI
  • Trigger initial load (for subsequent tests use delta replication - delta will be triggered if there are changes made in SuccessFactors)
  • Monitor SAP Cloud ALM for synchronization errors before proceeding with a broader rollout

Key Hints & Best Practices

  • Scheduling: Ensure the IPS job used to create the user core runs before MDI. The IPS job responsible for provisioning Approver roles must run after MDI — this can be the same job used for user core provisioning or a separate dedicated job. Sequencing is critical to avoid provisioning failures.
  • Monitoring: Actively monitor both IPS jobs and SAP Cloud ALM for errors. Error logs are not displayed in the Concur UI, so external monitoring is the only way to detect and resolve issues in a timely manner.
  • Troubleshooting: When engaging SAP Concur support for error analysis, always provide:
    • The Correlation ID of the request
    • The timeframe of the issue (a date is sufficient if Correlation ID is present)
    • A downloaded copy of the error message

Conclusion

Master Data Integration (MDI) provides a modern and standardized approach to synchronizing master data between SAP SuccessFactors and SAP Concur. By centralizing data distribution and leveraging SAP Cloud ALM (CALM) for monitoring and observability, organizations can improve data consistency, simplify integration management, and reduce administrative effort.

A successful implementation depends on three key factors: establishing a solid identity provisioning process with IAS and IPS, ensuring the correct sequence of user creation and role assignment, and defining accurate mappings for expense-related master data.

When implementing MDI, it is recommended to begin with a small pilot group, closely monitor synchronization jobs in IPS and SAP Cloud ALM, and fine-tune mappings and scheduling before expanding the integration to the entire organization. Following these best practices will help you build a reliable, scalable, and maintainable integration that provides a strong foundation for SAP Concur travel and expense processes.

entry.title: E-invoicing solution for France: Implementation Approach for Customers and Partners
entry.content:
E-invoicing solution for France: Implementation Approach for Customers and Partners

 

Introduction

This post provides technical guidance for implementing the French e‑invoicing (e‑facturation) solution with SAP Concur, focusing on a pull‑based integration pattern with external partners. For background and implementation options, see:

Prepare for France’s New E-Invoicing Requirements ... - SAP Concur Community.

Configuring France - External Integration Partners | SAP Help Portal

Note: This article focuses on the integration mechanics rather than the functional configuration, which is documented in the SAP Help Portal.

 

Solution approach - PULL model

 

 

Solution from SAP Concur

1.      Introduction of Standard Fields on Expense entry level

To support e‑invoice retrieval, SAP Concur introduces the following standard, editable fields at the expense entry level:

  • Merchant Tax ID
  • Invoice ID

Employees can manually enter these values when creating an expense entry.

 

2.      Trigger for External Partner Integration

When creating an expense entry, the employee must:

  • Provide Merchant Tax ID and Invoice ID
  • Upload the receipt in one of the supported formats: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .pdf, .tif, or .tiff

Upon clicking “Save,” Concur emits an external event to notify subscribed partners that:

  • An expense entry has been created, and
  • The corresponding e-invoice should be retrieved

This event‑based mechanism delivers a near real‑time experience. The expense report remains in “processing” until the partner responds by calling the API with the e‑invoice document.

 

Sample payload - ESS notification received to the webhook for the event :

{

    "id": "removed-for-security-reasons",

    "correlationId": "removed-for-security-reasons",

    "eventType": "FR.compliance",

    "topic": "public.concur.document.tax.compliance",

    "timeStamp": "2026-08-24T11:24:14.922Z",

    "data": null,

    "facts": {

        "companyId": "removed-for-security-reasons",

        "isDisplayVersionRequired": false,

        "isComplianceDocRequired": true,

        "taxId": "Tax123D",

        "complianceCountryCode": "FR",

        "documentId": "removed-for-security-reasons",

        "invoiceId": "123456ABCDE",

        "href": "https://eu2.api.concursolutions.com/document-compliance-gateway/v4/tax-documents/<documentId>"

    },

    "groups": null,

    "scopes": null

}

 

3.      Inbound Data from Partner

Using the Invoice ID + Merchant Tax ID combination, the partner locates, pulls, and sends the e‑invoice to Concur in XML or Factur‑X (PDF/A‑3) format.

  • The PUT request payload must include both the .xml and a .json (as described in “Payload” in the SAP Concur Developer Center | Document Compliance Gateway v4).
  • The API can also accept additional tokens such as amount and date (parsed by the partner from the XML).
  • The .json does not need to replicate all XML fields. Mandatory fields are defined in the schema provided in SAP Concur Developer Center | Document Compliance Gateway v4.

 

4.      Expense and Invoice Linking

Once received, the e‑invoice document is automatically linked to the corresponding expense entry. The receipt status changes to “E‑invoice certified,” after which the employee can submit the expense report.

 

 

Technical Steps for Partner Integration:

 

1.      Create a dedicated app, assign necessary scopes

Customers with Client Web Services can create App IDs and Client Secrets as described in “OAuth 2.0 Application Management Tool” (SAP Concur Developer Center).

SAP Concur Developer Center | OAuth 2.0 Application Management Tool

 

2.      Authentication

Follow  SAP Concur Developer Center | OAuth2 - Getting Started for token acquisition and

 

3.      Event subscription

 

Partners must subscribe to the event and expose an endpoint to receive notifications.

  • See the SAP Concur Developer Center | Event Subscription Service v4 Guide for step‑by‑step instructions.
  • Subscription steps are outlined in SAP Concur Developer Center | Event Subscription Service v4
  • Event details are documented under SAP Concur Developer Center | Document Tax Compliance Event For France, use eventType: FR.compliance.

 

4.      Implement Document Compliance Gateway API to accept XML document and token data

Use SAP Concur Developer Center | Document Compliance Gateway v4 to transmit the e‑invoice retrieved from the Portail Public de Facturation. Supported formats:

  • UBL 2.1 XML
  • UN/CEFACT CII XML
  • Factur X (PDF/A 3 with embedded XML)

Ensure your payload adheres to the v4 API schema and includes required JSON fields alongside the XML.

 

Adopting a pull‑based integration with SAP Concur enables partners to retrieve and submit French e‑invoices reliably and near real time, minimizing manual effort for employees and helping organizations comply with France’s evolving e‑invoicing requirements. The key success factors are:

  • Capturing Merchant Tax ID and Invoice ID at expense entry creation
  • Subscribing correctly to the FR.compliance event
  • Implementing the Document Compliance Gateway v4 with both XML and JSON payload components
  • Validating against the mandatory schema fields

By following the steps outlined above—app registration, OAuth2 authentication, event subscription, and compliant payload construction—customers and partners can streamline e‑invoice retrieval from the Portail Public de Facturation and achieve a smooth, auditable linkage between expenses and certified e‑invoices.

entry.title: How SAP users shape SAP products, and how you can too
entry.content:
The best product improvements start with real user feedback – like yours. No matter which SAP product or solution you use or how much experience you have, your feedback can help us create better experiences for users like you. In the past 18 months, more than 11,000 SAP users have joined the SAP User Research Panel, contributing to 80+ research studies that help shape SAP products used by millions of users.

As a panel member, you may be invited to take part in anonymous research studies, such as:

  • Surveys
  • Usability tests
  • Interviews

Studies are remote and take 30 minutes to one hour to complete.

Want to help shape what’s next?
Join the SAP User Research Panel.

From registration to the SAP User Research Panel to product impact. Alt text: Overview of the SAP User Research Panel journey, from registration and invitations to participation and product impact.

From registration to real product impact

Here are two examples of how SAP User Research Panel participants have helped improve SAP products and how your feedback can make a difference too.

Simplifying the SAP Concur Homepage

The SAP Concur homepage plays a central role in users' day-to-day experience. As part of the homepage redesign for approximately 12 million business travelers using SAP Concur each month, the product team gathered feedback through a 30-minute study with users.

This resulted in three key opportunities:

  • Make important information easier to find
  • Reduce the time spent on travel booking
  • Surface relevant information before users need to search for it

Using these insights, the team identified the changes that would deliver the greatest value to users. This resulted in a significant homepage redesign in the beginning of 2026, reducing 20 action buttons to five primary actions for a more focused, intuitive experience.

The first screenshot below, showing a specific customer configuration, illustrates that the primary actions—Create Request, Plan a Trip, Create Expense Report, and Request Cash Advance—are now directly visible rather than hidden under the Create button, as shown in the second screenshot.

As customers felt the banner image took up too much space, the new design uses it as a backdrop for the salutation and call-to-actions (CTAs) instead.


The previous SAP Concur homepage.


The new SAP Concur homepage as of January 2026.

The insights helped shape the development of a new company policy feature, which is now in the Early Adoption program with select customers.

“What we’re going to ship will ultimately provide value to our users.”
-- Arjun Ram, SAP Concur Product Manager

Helping shape the future of SAP Signavio

Panel participants have also influenced strategic product decisions for SAP Signavio.

One of the panel’s most popular studies explored the emerging topic of object-centric process mining, or OCPM. In a 10-minute survey, participants shared their familiarity with OCPM and related graph query languages.

The results were clear:

  • 95% of respondents were unfamiliar with Cypher
  • 88% had no knowledge of SPARQL

These insights helped the product team refine its implementation approach, making sure the planned solution better aligns with users’ existing knowledge and expectations.

 

Participants reported low levels of proficiency in both SPARQL and Cypher.

 

Your voice matters

Join the SAP User Research Panel and help improve the SAP products you use every day too.

As a panel member, you can:

  • Receive invitations to research studies that match your experience
  • Take part in 20–60-minute remote sessions
  • Share feedback to shape SAP products
  • Earn points when you join the SAP User Research Panel through the SAP Customer Appreciation Network

Learn more about the SAP User Research Panel.

We look forward to hearing from you!

entry.title: KSeF Poland E-Invoicing: Issuing Invoices to SAP Concur with Employee Details
entry.content:
KSeF Poland E-Invoicing: Issuing Invoices to SAP Concur with Employee Details

Overview

This document provides step-by-step instructions for accessing the KSeF 2.0 Test Portal, creating a test invoice, and maintaining employee contact information within the invoice. Correct completion of these fields ensures that employee details are displayed appropriately in the generated invoice.

Accessing the KSeF 2.0 Test Portal

Test Portal URL:
ap-test.ksef.mf.gov.pl

Login Procedure

 

  1. Open the Portal

    • Launch the KSeF Test Taxpayer Application using the URL above.

  2. Select the Company Identifier

    • Choose NIP firmy (Company Tax Identification Number) as the identifier type.
    • Enter the applicable Polish Tax Identification Number (NIP).

  3. Select an Authentication Method

    • Choose one of the available authentication options:

      • Certyfikat kwalifikowany (Qualified Certificate)

      • Pieczęć NIP (NIP Seal)

      • Profil Zaufany (Trusted Profile)

    Note: For testing purposes, a test NIP number may be used for authentication.

Invoice Creation Process

After a successful login, proceed with invoice creation as follows:

  • Page 1: Enter the invoice details.
  • Page 2: Enter the buyer information.
  • Page 3: Enter the seller information.
  • Page 4: Maintain additional entity and contact information.

Upon reaching Page 4, the application will display the section shown in the corresponding screenshot.

 

Configuring Employee Details

To associate an employee with the invoice, complete the following steps:

Step 1: Select the Appropriate Entity Type

  • Select "Not" and navigate to the Other Entity Details section.
  • This section allows employee information to be maintained and linked to the invoice.
 

 

Step 2: Complete the Employee Information

Populate the fields using the following values:

Field Value
RoleEmployee
Identification DataNo ID
NameEmployee First Name and Last Name
AddressNo

Step 3: Maintain Contact Information

  1. Navigate to the Contact Details section.
  2. Select Add Contact Details.
  3. Enter the employee's SAP email address.

 

Expected Outcome

When all information is entered correctly:

  • The invoice will display "Podmiot Inny 1" (Other Entity 1).
  • The employee will be listed under the selected entity.
  • The employee's SAP email address will be displayed within the Contact Details section.
  • The invoice structure will reflect the employee information exactly as required for testing and validation purposes.

 

Conclusion

Following the above procedure ensures that employee information is correctly maintained within the KSeF 2.0 test invoice. Proper configuration of the Other Entity Details and Contact Details sections is essential for validating how employee contact information is represented in the generated invoice.
